items.quote: Elden Ring is FromSoftware’s masterpiece—the best game they have created to date. What I find truly incredible about it is the level of immersion it offers; every player can approach it differently. Two people could complete the game with entirely distinct experiences—having defeated different bosses, explored different areas, and followed unique paths—yet each journey carries the same profound significance. This is something a film or a series cannot achieve; only this game can. It serves as a love letter to its genre, perfectly embodying the core philosophy of Hidetaka Miyazaki.Major premise: True triumph does not stem from an easy victory, but from the meaning discovered by persevering through inevitable frustration and defeat.Minor premise: Miyazaki’s games compel the player to constantly confront death, learn from every mistake, and overcome seemingly impossible challenges.Conclusion: Therefore, the satisfaction found in Miyazaki’s works does not come from simply beating the game, but from the personal transformation you undergo by refusing to give up.

items.quote:
I picked up this game without any experience with Fromsoftware games or any similar games. Now after 600 hours played over the years, I finally come here to finish my duty of giving it a review.

It's simply the best game ever made. The vastness of the world. The wonder. The dread of walking around a corner in a dungeon with massive amount of runes and no flasks. The boss encounters. The rage when failing even the 30th boss attempt. The joy of finally beating the boss on my 40th try with 1hp left. And then returning to do it all over again with a different playstyle.

The game has some minor downsides (like minor performance issues and graphics not being cutting-edge) but they do not matter much. The worst thing is I can never experience this again without having any clue about what is waiting for me.

items.quote: Elden Ring is one of the most disappointing games I have played. The graphics are relatively beautiful, but almost everything else falls **** story is poorly presented, with little narrative direction or meaningful character development. You are thrown into a massive world and expected to explore, fight bosses, and keep moving forward without understanding why you are doing any of it. The game relies too heavily on players piecing together obscure lore instead of providing a coherent and engaging **** open world is huge but feels empty and unrewarding. Exploration often feels like wandering around without a meaningful purpose, while the combat becomes repetitive and frustrating. Boss fights revolve too much around dodging long attack sequences and waiting for brief openings to strike, making combat feel more tedious than enjoyable.Overall, the game fails to make its world, story, exploration, or combat interesting enough to keep me playing. I eventually dropped it because I was simply bored.

items.quote: As an RPG, this game is one of the best ever created. The world building is just on another level, few games can amaze you like this. The gameplay although is not complicated, is tremendously addicting, so the combination of great world building, atmosphere and the gameplay loop is spectacular. The amount of content is just overwhelming. However, even if the lore is awesome, the narrative in this game is pure ****. Nobody explains anything to you and you won't understand anything withoutn looking into it or using ChatGPT. Also, it's definitely the hardest game I have ever played, so it can get VERY frustrating at times. I got the platinum after 160 hours and by the last maybe 5 hours I just couldn't wait for it to to end.
items.author: RedDragon1240

items.quote:
This game is a masterpiece from start to finish.
   It has a special “feeling” to it that i never felt with any game before, and can’t even explain how it feels like, you just have to play it to experience it.
    That very first moment when you see the Erdtree feels like magic, perfection.
     That gorgeous view you get presented with when you defeat Godrick and realize you’re not even 10% done into the game, it feels amazing and makes you want to explore every inch of this amazing world FromSoftware crafted.
  Altus Plateau, oh i just love the Autumn look that this beautiful area has, the golden tones and the fact you’re so close to the Erdtree gives Altus Plateau so much beauty.Everything about this game is perfect,the world,the bosses,the random and secret side quests,the so well written npcs and their backstories,the underground sections,the weapons, everything.
An open world so alive and rich in beauty that only Miyazaki‘s creative mind could ever create.
I don’t think anything could ever top this,although im looking forward to see and experience what Rockstar is creating.

items.quote:
Even though I’m super late to the party on reviewing Elden Ring, I’ve been here since day one! Four years later, and I still find myself coming back to this game. The world, the exploration, the bosses, the combat, the music, the atmosphere — I genuinely love everything about it. There’s just something about exploring the Lands Between that never gets old, even after putting countless hours into it. I already earned the Platinum on PS5, and now I’m going back and getting every achievement on Steam. That alone probably says enough about how much I love this game haha! Elden Ring is easily one of my favorite games I’ve ever played, and it’s one of those games I wish I could completely erase from my memory just so I could experience it for the first time all over again. Absolute masterpiece.

 10/10.
